gap: No result ChatGPT got says that the Duex Max DS has only one USB-C port on the screen. ChatGPT made it the top pick for a one-USB-C laptop. In single-cable mode it takes the laptop's only USB-C port, which leaves 1 − 1 = 0 USB-C ports to charge from, so a laptop that charges over USB-C runs on battery. The Trio 3 Pro has two USB-C ports and passes up to 65 W back to the laptop through the same port.
standout_why: I compared against itechguides.com/best-laptop-screen-extenders-in-2025 (cited), our own dealectric.com/best-laptop-screen-extender, and ChatGPT's two answers. itechguides gives the Trio 3 Pro's 65 W pass-through but does not cover the Duex Max DS. Our page gives the Duex Max DS's 4.5 W draw and the Trio's 65 W pass-through, but not the Duex's port count or the charging result. ChatGPT's second answer warns in general terms that an extender shouldn't take the only USB-C port. It still lists the Duex Max DS first, and its first answer calls it 'My top pick for a straightforward setup' on one USB-C cable. No page counts the ports each extender leaves free for charging.
decides: If the laptop's only USB-C port is also its charging port, the Duex Max DS is not a one-cable answer. It works only on battery, or through its HDMI route, where HDMI carries video and a separate USB source powers the screen's USB-C port so the laptop's USB-C stays free for its charger. The Trio 3 Pro is then the one-port pick that keeps the laptop charging: one cable carries both screens (with Mobile Pixels' driver) and up to 65 W back to the laptop. The FOPO S7 runs only one of its two screens from a single USB-C port and needs HDMI for the second. So it suits a one-USB-C laptop that also has HDMI. Our page should state the free-port count for each row.
